page: Amazon Web Services r7a.large is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor with x86_64 architecture, providing 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score both placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong. However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance metrics, such as the Geekbench multi-core score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, fall into the bottom 25%, reflecting the low core count of this specific instance size. Memory bandwidth read-only tests and database operations also register in the lower 25%, while write bandwidth and text processing perform at average levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7a.large offers a modern DDR5 memory architecture and dedicated AMD EPYC cores at a lower entry point within the r7a family, making it suitable for memory-sensitive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. Given the high memory-to-core ratio combined with strong single-core performance but weaker multi-core and database throughput, this instance is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive applications, single-threaded data processing, caching layers, and basic web serving.
